internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all three attestations fjj is a concrete geographic word for an open way through the land that people travel by. It appears twice paired with the ordinary word for 'ways' (subul) — once as the noun 'passes' (21:31 'fijaAjan subulan') and once as the adjective 'broad' describing those ways (71:20 'subulan fijaAjan') — and once as a singular head-noun 'from every deep/remote faj' (22:27). The pairing with, and modification of, subul shows fjj is not merely a synonym for 'road': it is the open passage/route, or the broad-open quality of a route. The evidence is fully coherent but thin (3 tokens, purely noun/adjective, one physical domain, no verb).
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: NOT the generic 'way/road' itself (that is subul/sabIl, which fjj co-occurs with in 21:31 and 71:20 and attributively modifies in 71:20 — a word cannot be synonymous with the noun it qualifies). NOT metaphorical or moral (no 'sabIl Allah'-type sense; strictly physical-geographic in all 3, even where guidance yahtaduun appears in 21:31, where the fijaAj are only the physical means, not the guidance). NOT human-constructed roads (natural features God 'placed in' the earth, jaEalnaA fIhaA, paired with mountains). NOT inherently narrow/enclosed (the attributive pull is toward open/broad; where remoteness is meant a separate qualifier EamIq is supplied in 22:27). NO verbal/eventive/abstract sense is attested; any etymological 'split/open/gush' core cannot be imported (that frame belongs to a distinct root, fjr, and must not be conflated).
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 22:27:13:1 'min kulli faj~in EamIqin' — the only singular, only non-subul-paired token, and the salient qualifier is EamIq ('deep/remote'), not width. Against any account that makes breadth CRITERIAL this resists: 'broad' does no work here. It is resolved by demoting breadth to a foregrounded-but-optional nuance (broad in 71:20, deep in 22:27) and setting the essential core at 'traversable open passage/route through terrain,' which 22:27 satisfies as a deep/remote pass. No occurrence resists that core.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: That fjj is a bare synonym of subul ('way/road'). Refuted Quran-internally: in 71:20 'subulan fijaAjan' fjj is the ADJ modifying subul, and in 21:31 the two nouns appear together — synonymy would make one redundant, and a word cannot modify its own synonym. A secondary competitor — that fjj is a pure dimensional property ('broad'/openness), with the noun a substantivization — is refuted by 22:27, where faj~ is a singular head-noun with its own dimension (qualified by EamIq), an entity not a mere adjective. rejection_condition.verification_method: Confirm the QAC morphology (qac_pos / qac_verb_form) and read the full verse_text; test whether replacing fjj with subul preserves meaning (synonymy test) and whether the token carries motion/eventivity itself rather than via co-verbs (yaAtI, taslukuu).
